extra.message: The gateway CORS filter reflects the request's Origin header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true while allowing all requested headers. Any website can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses, enabling account data theft/CSRF-style attacks.

extra.message: The mapper uses MyBatis string substitution ${userId} instead of a bound parameter #{userId} in the WHERE clause of listEmployeeByUserId. This bypasses JDBC parameterization and is a SQL-injection pattern; it must use #{userId}.

extra.message: The upload path is built from the request-supplied FileUploadVO.bizType (via AbstractFileStrategy.getPath) without any validation, then joined with the storage root. A bizType such as '../../../../tmp/x' (URL-decoded) escapes the storage directory and lets an attacker write an uploaded file to an arbitrary filesystem location. Only the original filename is checked for '../', not bizType.
